Franz Kernel User ABI Definitions

Description: Master Application Binary Interface (ABI) definitions, system call offsets, and execution macros for the Franz RISC-V user environment.

ABI Base & Block Offsets
ABI_BASE The master ABI pointer.​ The kernel pre-loads the base

address (0x80201000) into this register.

Registers:

s1 : Holds the base pointer. Users MUST NOT modify this register if they intend to use the kcall macros.

B0_OFF Block 0 Base Offset (0x000) - I/O & Multimedia.
B1_OFF Block 1 Base Offset (0x800) - CPU & Time (2048).
B2_OFF Block 2 Base Offset (0x1000) - Memory & Data (4096).
B3_OFF Block 3 Base Offset (0x1800) - Platform API (6144).
Block 0 - I/O & Multimedia
UART_PUTC Offset: B0_OFF + 0x000.​ Prints a single character.
UART_PUTS Offset: B0_OFF + 0x008.​ Prints a string.
UART_PUTHEX Offset: B0_OFF + 0x010.​ Prints a hexadecimal value.
UART_PUTDEC Offset: B0_OFF + 0x018.​ Prints a decimal value.
UART_GETC Offset: B0_OFF + 0x020.​ Retrieves a single character

from input.

PX_GETW Offset: B0_OFF + 0x200.​ Gets pixel buffer width.
PX_GETH Offset: B0_OFF + 0x208.​ Gets pixel buffer height.
PX_BUFFER Offset: B0_OFF + 0x210.​ Retrieves pixel buffer pointer.
PX_SYNC Offset: B0_OFF + 0x218.​ Synchronizes the pixel buffer with

the display.

SND_SET Offset: B0_OFF + 0x400.​ Configures audio settings.
NET_SUPPORT Offset: B0_OFF + 0x600.​ Checks or configures network

availability.

Block 1 - CPU & Time
SYS_TIME Offset: B1_OFF + 0x000.​ Retrieves system time.
SYS_CYCLES Offset: B1_OFF + 0x008.​ Retrieves CPU cycle count.
SYS_DELAY_US Offset: B1_OFF + 0x010.​ Delays execution in

microseconds.

SYS_FREQ Offset: B1_OFF + 0x018.​ Retrieves CPU frequency.
SYS_CPUID Offset: B1_OFF + 0x020.​ Retrieves the ID of the executing

core.

SYS_FENCEI Offset: B1_OFF + 0x028.​ Executes an instruction memory

fence.

SYS_TIMER_SET Offset: B1_OFF + 0x030.​ Configures a hardware timer.
SYS_ISA Offset: B1_OFF + 0x038.​ Retrieves ISA support flags.
SYS_HALT Offset: B1_OFF + 0x040.​ Halts the system or execution

context.

Block 2 - Memory & Data (Fast Memory Ops)
MEM_COPY Offset: B2_OFF + 0x000.​ Fast memory copy operation.
Registers:

a0 : Destination pointer (dst).  - a1 : Source pointer (src).  - a2 : Length in bytes (len).

MEM_SET Offset: B2_OFF + 0x008.​ Fills memory with a specific

byte value.

Registers:

a0 : Destination pointer (dst).  - a1 : Value to set (val).  - a2 : Length in bytes (len).

MEM_COMPARE Offset: B2_OFF + 0x010.​ Compares two memory regions.
Registers:

a0 : First memory pointer (ptr1). Returns the comparison result

here.

a1 : Second memory pointer (ptr2).  - a2 : Length in bytes (len).

MEM_MOVE Offset: B2_OFF + 0x018.​ Overlap-safe memory copy.
Registers:

a0 : Destination pointer (dst).  - a1 : Source pointer (src).  - a2 : Length in bytes (len).

STR_LEN Offset: B2_OFF + 0x020.​ Calculates string length.
Registers:

a0 : String pointer (str_ptr). Returns the length here.

Block 2 - Memory & Data (Management & IPC)
MEM_TOTAL Offset: B2_OFF + 0x200.​ Retrieves total system RAM.​ Returns

in a0.

MEM_FREE Offset: B2_OFF + 0x208.​ Retrieves currently free

RAM. Returns in a0.

MEM_PAGE_SIZE Offset: B2_OFF + 0x210.​ Retrieves CPU page size

(usually 4KB). Returns in a0.

MB_READ Offset: B2_OFF + 0x400.​ Reads from the Node.​js Host Mailbox.
Registers:

a0 : Read offset.

MB_WRITE Offset: B2_OFF + 0x408.​ Writes to the Node.​js Host Mailbox.
Registers:

a0 : Write offset.  - a1 : Value to write.

MB_FLUSH Offset: B2_OFF + 0x410.​ Triggers host-side processing

for IPC.

FS_SYNC Offset: B2_OFF + 0x600.​ Commits all writes to disk

(OPFS/Geomancy hooks).

FS_STAT Offset: B2_OFF + 0x608.​ Retrieves storage health and status.
Block 3 - Platform API
PL_CH_MSG_GET Offset: B3_OFF + 0x000.​ Retrieves a platform channel

message.

PL_CH_MSG_SET Offset: B3_OFF + 0x008.​ Sets a platform channel

message.

PL_CH_MSG_NEW Offset: B3_OFF + 0x010.​ Instantiates a new platform

channel message.

System Execution Macros
KCALL Bypasses the 12-bit immediate limit of 'ld' by using 'li' and

'add', allowing offsets larger than 2047 bytes.

Parameters: offset

The predefined ABI offset constant (e.g., UART_PUTC).

Registers:

s1 : Read-only. Must contain the ABI base pointer (0x80201000).  -

t5 : Mutated. Used to load the 32-bit exact byte offset.

t6 : Mutated. Used

to calculate the target function pointer address.

ra : Mutated. Overwritten by the jalr (jump and link) instruction.

PLATFORM_WAIT Initiates a spin-loop, polling a memory address to

synchronize with the host platform. Hints to QEMU to save host energy if paused.

Registers:

t2 : Read-only. Expected to contain the pointer to the

synchronization flag.

t0 : Mutated. Used to load and evaluate the flag value from memory.

EXIT Wrapper for the SYS_HALT system call.​ Halts the current

context. Uses the KCALL register requirements.

Context Management Macros
PUSH_FRAME Allocates stack space and saves the return address (64-bit).
Parameters: space

The total byte size to allocate on the stack.

Registers:

sp : Mutated. Stack pointer is decremented by the requested space.  - ra : Read-only. Stored onto the newly allocated stack frame.

POP_FRAME Restores the return address and deallocates stack space

(64-bit).

Parameters: space

The total byte size to deallocate from the stack.

Registers:

sp : Mutated. Stack pointer is incremented by the requested space.  - ra : Mutated. Restored from the stack frame.

SAVE_ALL Saves all 32 general-purpose registers to the stack.​ Total

size footprint is 256 bytes (32 registers * 8 bytes).

Registers:

sp : Mutated. Used to store context. The original SP is saved

to mscratch and eventually written to stack offset 8 (x2 slot).

mscratch

Mutated. Temporarily holds the original SP during the save operation.  -

x1, x3-x31 : Read-only. All general-purpose registers are pushed to the stack.

RESTORE_ALL Restores all 32 general-purpose registers from the stack

frame and cleans up the 256-byte allocation.

Registers:

sp : Mutated. Incremented by 256 bytes after restoration.  - t0 : Mutated. Used to read the original SP from the stack and write it back

to mscratch.

mscratch : Mutated. Restored to hold the original SP.  - x1, x3-x31 : Mutated. Completely overwritten with values from the stack frame.
